statement.p: We already know we can do the following problem using u-substitution, with u = \sin(13 x )

We see that \displaystyle \int \sin^{12} (13 x) \cos^3(13 x) \,dx \ is solved similarly, because
the exponent of \cos is odd.
the exponent of \sin is odd.
None of the above
So we'll still use u-substitution with u = \sin(13 x ), after first rewriting \cos^3 (13 x) = \cos^2(13 x) \cos(13 x ) and using a trig identity.
Select the trigonometric identity needed to solve this problem.
Finally, put it all together to calculate \displaystyle \int \sin^{12}\mathopen{}\left(13x\right)\cos^{3}\mathopen{}\left(13x\right) \,dx \ = \

hint.p: The integral involves \sin u and \cos u where the exponent of \cos u is an odd, positive integer, namely, 3. So we factor out a copy of \cos(13 x) and use the identity \sin^2 u + \cos^2 u = 1 to turn the remaining \cos^2(13 x) into an expression involving \sin^2(13 x).

Thus the integral can be rewritten as \int \sin^{12}\mathopen{}\left(13x\right)\cos^{3}\mathopen{}\left(13x\right) \, dx = \int \sin^{12} (13 x) \cos^2(13 x) \cos(13 x) \, dx = \int \sin^{12} (13 x) \bigg(1-\sin^2(13 x)\bigg) \cos(13 x) \, dx and we use u-substitution.
Letting u= \sin (13 x) so du = 13 \cos (13 x) \, dx and thus \displaystyle dx = \frac{ du}{13 \cos (13 x)}.

This turns the integral into \int u^{12} (1-u^2) \cos(13 x) \, \frac{ du}{13 \cos (13 x)} = \frac{1}{13}\int u^{12} (1-u^2) \, du which can be multiplied out, and then each part integrated by power rule.

solution.p: We factor out a copy of \cos(13 x) and use the identity \sin^2 u + \cos^2 u = 1 to turn the remaining \cos^2(13 x) into an expression involving \sin^2(13 x).
Then we use u-substitution, letting u= \sin (13 x) so du = 13 \cos (13 x) \, dx and thus \displaystyle dx = \frac{ du}{13 \cos (13 x)}.

p.me: \begin{aligned} \int \sin^{12}\mathopen{}\left(13x\right)\cos^{3}\mathopen{}\left(13x\right) \, dx \amp = \int \sin^{12} (13 x) \cos^2(13 x) \cos(13 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = \int \sin^{12} (13 x) \bigg(1-\sin^2(13 x)\bigg) \cos(13 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = \int u^{12} (1-u^2) \cos(13 x) \, \frac{ du}{13 \cos (13 x)} \\\\ \amp = \frac{1}{13}\int u^{12} (1-u^2) \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{1}{13}\int u^{12} -u^{14} \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{1}{13} \left[ \frac{u^{13}}{13} - \frac{u^{15}}{15} \right]+C \\\\ \amp = \frac{1}{13} \left[ \frac{\sin^{13}(13 x) }{13} - \frac{\sin^{15}(13 x)}{15} \right]+C \\\\ \end{aligned}

solution.p: The correct trigonometric identity used is E.
